relationships.subject: Nav1.8+ nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: Genetic ablation of nociceptors fully abrogated reinnervation allodynia.

relationships.subject: spared nerve injury
relationships.evidence_quote: fibres invading the tibial territory in conjunction with the emergence of neuropathic pain are nociceptors sprouting as collaterals from the neighbouring, intact sural nerve

relationships.subject: collateral sprouting
relationships.evidence_quote: This reinnervation-induced neuropathic pain involved nociceptors that sprouted into denervated territories precisely reproducing the initial pattern of innervation, were guided by blood vessels and showed irregular terminal connectivity in the skin and lowered activation thresholds mimicking low-threshold afferents.

relationships.subject: blood vessels
relationships.evidence_quote: implicate blood vessels in providing a scaffold for collaterally sprouting nociceptors in denervated tissue

relationships.subject: Nav1.8+ nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: low-threshold afferents-which normally mediate touch sensation as well as allodynia in intact nerve territories after injury<sup>4-7</sup>-did not reinnervate, leading to an aberrant innervation of tactile end organs such as Meissner corpuscles with nociceptors alone

key_findings: After SNI, denervated skin initially lost sensation then developed late-onset allodynia and aversion to touch (~20 weeks) as Nav1.8+ nociceptors from the intact sural nerve collaterally sprouted into it, while Aβ-LTMRs never reinnervated.

Sprouting nociceptors followed blood vessels, failed to form intra-epidermal endings, aberrantly innervated Meissner corpuscles and acquired low thresholds; genetic ablation of nociceptors abolished reinnervation allodynia.
